Vs.
Md Mahbubey Alam and others  ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 8. The plaintiff-respondents instituted the suit for declaration of title by adverse possession and a consequential relief for a decree that the notices issued under section 64(1) of the Ordinance for eviction of the plaintiffs is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiffs on the averment, inter alia, that one Peer Box Sawdagar was the original owner of the suit land which was inherited by the predecessor of the plaintiffs Yakub Sawdagar by way of purchase on 24-2-1932 and have possessed mutating his name in the Sherista of the Zaminder and paying rent regularly and constructed a pucca building and planted trees, made pucca wall in the suit land. The father of the appellant-defendant No.1, however, instituted the suit for declaration that the property belonged to and was part of Amir Ali Waqf Estate and also for resovery of khas possession by evicting the present plaintiffs predecessor Yakub Sb. and grand-mother Fida Bibi therefrom. The suit being Title Suit No. 929 of 1931 was decreed on 22-8-1934 and an appeal therefrom being Title Appeal No. 375 of 1935 was dismissed on 19-8-1935. The second appeal being Second Appeal No. 1192 of 1937 was, however, dismissed on 27-7-1939 but the predecessor of the defendant never took possession by way of execution of the decree or otherwise evicting the plaintiffs predecessor and grandmother therefrom. The predecessor of the plaintiffs accordingly, continued in their possession in the suit land as before on payment of rent and after State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the suit land was recorded in the name of plaintiffs father without any objection from any quarter whatsoever and subsequently, the name was recorded in the PS Khatian and the father of the plaintiffs has been possessing on payment of rent and taxes to different authorities. Upon the death of the plaintiff's father in 1965 the plaintiffs as the heirs have been owning and possessing the suit land openly and adversely without any interference or interruption from any quarter and upon amicable arrangement between the plaintiffs and the deceased father, the plaintiff became the sole owner and being in possession mutated the same in his name in the record of right overruling the objections of the defendants upto appellate stage. The defendants. ultimately, took a short-cut measure issuing notices under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance terming the plaintiffs as illegal occupants of the waqf property without serving any notice whatsoever and hence the suit.
